ISSUES: Rating applies GST at 18% (CGST 9% + SGST 9%, or IGST 18%). Individual and family floater health policies are GST-exempt from 22 Sep 2025.
Keep the table-driven GST design; load 0% for this product. Confirm with the insurer's tax team whether any add-on (PA, CI) is taxed separately.
Three plans are named by age (<35, 36–55, >55) but no rule ties a plan to the customer's age; a 60-year-old can buy the <35 plan and its youth packages. Age 35 falls in no plan.
Add NEW-PLN-01: plan by eldest member's age (floater) or each member's age (individual): Young up to 35, Prime 36–55, Senior 56+; Classic any age.

Four of the twelve preselected packages contain a cover with no approved premium (Mental Wellness in Young P1; Health Check-up Plus in Prime P2; Senior Care and Senior Health Check-up in Senior P3). Young P2 contains Personal Accident, which needs base SI above ₹10 L and family income above ₹10 L, so most young buyers cannot take the package as designed.
Plan Cover Relation; Coverage List; ATR_205
Remove unpriced covers from packages until rates are filed, and take PA out of Young P2 (offer it as a suggested cover). The live quote shows the effect.

The medical grid has gaps. No rule decides: ₹1 Cr at age 51–65; ₹50 L at 61–65; anything below ₹50 L at 61 and above; ₹2 Cr at 18–55; any SI above ₹1 Cr for children. No path exists for a declared, controlled PED: every STP rule requires 'no PED' and only heart and managed-care conditions have rules.
Adopt the completed grid (NEW-UW-02) and NEW-UW-01 for controlled PED (Tele-MER + underwriter, PED loading 5%–100%).

Overlapping and duplicate rules: BR-073 (above 66) and BR-132 (above 65) cover the same SI band with different outcomes; managed-care rules are duplicated with different referral teams (024/087, 025/088, 026/089, 030/093); BR-129 (46–55) and BR-131 (55–65) both include age 55.
Merge duplicates and name one referral team per condition; use non-overlapping age bands (46–54, 55–65).

Zone is defined four ways: rate and code tables Zone 1–7 plus 'No'; clause CL-008 Zone A–D; BR-125 Zone 1–4. The field says zone is derived from PIN and cannot be changed, CL-008 lets the customer choose a higher zone, and BR-049 asks the user to select one. Zones 3–7 share one factor (0.95).
Fields; ClauseList; Rules; Rate Tables D
One zone model: Zone 1–7 from the PIN master, no manual override except a priced upgrade to a higher zone; delete 'No'; correct CL-008 and BR-125.

Room rent is defined three ways: in-patient attribute (below ₹10 L: 1% of SI; ₹10 L+: up to Deluxe), Room Modification (up to ₹5 L: 1%, ICU 2%; ₹7.5 L+: up to Deluxe) and clause CL-007 (single private AC unless upgraded). At ₹7.5 L they give three answers. The specification's worked example rates ₹10 L on single private AC.
ATR_086; Fields (Room Modification); CL-007; Rating C.7
One table: up to ₹5 L 1% (ICU 2%), ₹7.5 L single private AC, ₹10 L+ up to Deluxe; room relativity defaults from it; fix CL-007 and the worked example.

Pre/post hospitalisation: base benefit fixed at 60/180 days; clause CL-019 says 60/90/120; the modification options give 12 combinations (pre 30/60/90 × post 60/90/120/180) but the rate table prices 7.
Limit the options to the 7 priced pairs, or have actuarial price all 12; align CL-019 to the default 60/180.

Loyalty bonus conflicts: CL-012 says 100% a year with unlimited accumulation; the benefit caps at 1000% (under 35) or 500%; a field says the annual rate is 10% for ₹3–4 L; the worked example uses 20%–100% instead of the default.
Clause wording follows the option chosen; default 100%–1000% under 35 and 100%–500% from 35; options for ₹3–4 L limited to low-accrual choices.
Reset is a mandatory clause with unlimited restorations (CL-010), yet the customer can pick 0, 1, 2 or unlimited restorations at a price. Claim rule says reset is not available with Unlimited SI.
Make restoration count a selectable base option with clause wording per option; suppress it for Unlimited SI.
BR-RHI-100 blocks any non-resident proposer, but the product grants a flat 15% NRI discount and BR-101 handles NRIs taking worldwide cover.
Decide: allow NRIs with an Indian address and a primary-residence declaration (keep BR-101 and the discount), or drop the NRI discount.

The NRI discount alone reaches the 15% cap, so NRIs get no other discount. Discount in lieu of commission (up to 15%) has no channel rule. An employee discount appears in BR-050 but not in the discount list. Early entry discount does not say whose age counts on a floater.
Add NEW-DIS-01 (in-lieu-of-commission only where no commission is paid), NEW-DIS-02 (early entry: every adult under 40 and no PED on the policy); add or delete the employee discount.

Child entry: 91 days (overview) vs 3 months / 90 days (BR-003); child maximum 35 (BR-004), well above the market norm of 25 for dependent children. No adult maximum entry age, but the age table ends at 95 and multi-year rating adds a year each policy year.
Child minimum 91 days; dependent child maximum 25 (confirm if 35 is intended); NEW-ELG-01: entry age + term − 1 ≤ 95.
POS sum insured cap conflicts: BR-063 says ₹5 L, BR-096 says ₹10 L.
Keep one cap per channel in a channel–SI table; confirm against the POS product guidelines.

'Policy Sum Insured' = base SI + every over-and-above add-on SI (PA, CI, maternity). Medical-grid and channel rules say 'Sum Insured' without saying which. A ₹10 L policy with ₹1 Cr PA would read as ₹1.1 Cr and trigger high-SI medicals.
Fields Policy Sum Insured; UW rules
All underwriting and channel rules read Base SI (NEW-SI-01); Policy SI is for display only.
'Unlimited' sum insured has no number. Reinsurance cession, treaty limits and capital need a monetary exposure.
Set a notional exposure for Unlimited SI for reinsurance and reporting; confirm with the reinsurance team.
Floater family relativity is keyed on 'proposer age group' (Section H) while base premium uses the eldest member's age (C.3). A child-only individual policy has no family-relativity row below 18.
Key every floater factor on the eldest member; use the 18–35 row for members under 18 (the live quote does this).

Voluntary co-pay and deductible discounts sit inside the base premium, so every percentage add-on (air ambulance, worldwide, consumables) is discounted too. The specification marks the add-on denominator as pending QA.
Decide whether add-ons follow cost-sharing. If not, compute the add-on base before co-pay and deductible.
PED loading is applied to the whole gross premium, including fixed add-ons (PA, Hospicash) that have no link to the declared condition.
Apply PED loading to base and percentage add-ons only, or confirm the current approach is intended.
Two add-on rate tables are empty (Critical Illness, Infertility/ART) and seven covers have premium 'pending'. If these covers are selectable at launch they are given free.
NEW-ELG-02: a cover with no approved rate cannot be selected; show it as 'coming soon'.
The open item about a maternity gap between ₹15 L and ₹20 L is not a real gap: no sum insured option lies between them. Maternity is available from ₹7.5 L.

Nominee level conflicts: v1.5 moved nominee to policy level; BIE-01 says nominee is per member; BR-037/038/059 check nominee per member; BIE-01-R1 allows up to 4 nominees with shares, but the field list holds one nominee.
Policy-level nominee list: up to 4 nominees, shares adding to 100%, appointee for minors.
Branch P4 refers to CAN-07, which is not defined. 'Policy Pause' is listed in the version history but not in the endorsement scenarios, although Travel Pause depends on it.
Define CAN-07 and the Policy Pause endorsement, or remove the references.

Renewal is out of MVP, but the product sells multi-year terms and benefits that only take effect at renewal: wellness premium return, premium lock, money back after 5 claim-free years, loyalty bonus, adventure sub-limit removal, early renewal discount.
Renewal must be live before the first annual policy renews (12 months after launch), or hide renewal-dependent covers at launch.
No clause or rule for the Customer Information Sheet, senior-citizen grievance handling or the cashless turnaround (1 hour pre-authorisation, 3 hours discharge).

External integrations are not specified although fields and rules depend on outside systems: PIN/zone master, CKYC, Tele-MER and pre-policy check-up vendors, wellness vendor, TPA, payment (UPI autopay / NACH), health ID card, document dispatch.
Specify each interface (Integrations tab) before build.
Live-in partner (same or opposite sex) is in the relationship master, but floater and maternity rules name only 'spouse'.
NEW-ELG-04: treat live-in partner as spouse for floater, maternity and discount rules.
2X SI at Day 1 has no rate for Unlimited SI and no rule stopping it; No-Limit cover is already suppressed for Unlimited.
NEW-ELG-03: 2X SI not available with Unlimited SI.
Daily and weekly instalments are added but on hold. Combined with the 15-day grace and auto-cancellation for unpaid instalments, they would create very high collection and servicing volumes.
Launch with yearly to monthly only; review daily and weekly after six months of collection data.
Bariatric surgery is a base cover on every plan but is available only for SI of ₹5 L and above; nothing says what applies at ₹3–4 L.
State that bariatric surgery is excluded below ₹5 L, with the clause wording to match.
The design's own gap list is empty and the plan names in the overview are out of date.
Use the Issues tab as the gap list; correct the overview.
